analysis.primary_table: CUDA forward GEMM and complete backward, bias=False, cached FP8 weights, default RTX5090 configurations; no RTX PRO 6000 tile tuning.
analysis.numeric_validation: All five benchmark cases have bitwise-identical forward/dX/dW versus Triton. Maximum relative L2 bias-gradient error is below 1e-7.
analysis.portability_fix: Added explicit <cstdint> include to vendored ThunderKittens common/base_types.cuh for GCC13. CUDA arithmetic and tile configurations are unchanged.
analysis.phase_timing_caveat: Components are measured independently with warm buffers, so their sum need not equal a complete phase; similarly, isolated weight-refresh latency need not equal its incremental cost in a refresh+forward+backward graph.
analysis.small_case: Smallest dX grid has only16 CTAs and dW64, below188 SMs; launch and occupancy limitations matter.
analysis.large_case: Current CUDA kernels outperform Triton substantially, but effective FP8a32 MFU remains well below the supplied peak range. Timings alone do not identify a hardware bottleneck.
analysis.public_module: The public FP8Linear(backward_backend="cuda") still uses Triton forward. The primary CUDA-forward numbers use the independent CUDA GEMM plan; module_triton_forward_cuda_backward is the corresponding preallocated kernel combination, not a measurement of Python/autograd overhead.
